The lamp went out at the worst possible hour.

Nell counted the waves while she waited for her father to come back up the tower stairs. Nine. Ten. The wind pushed at the glass like something with shoulders.

"You will have to go," her sister said at last.

***

So she went, one hand on the cold rail, the other holding the spare wick against her chest as if it were a bird.
